claims.text: The initial equiatomic FeCoNi alloy is a single-phase fcc material with high saturation magnetization and low coercivity.
Roughly 50 at.% Pt can be introduced while retaining a FeCoNi-based high-entropy composition with configurational entropy of at least 1.0R.
Rapid thermal annealing of the Pt-modified FeCoNi alloy will induce L10 chemical ordering.
The Pt-modified and annealed FeCoNi alloy will form a single ordered L10 phase with tetragonal symmetry.
Pt addition reduces lattice symmetry and thereby promotes L10 ordering.
The lower symmetry of the L10 phase increases magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
The increased anisotropy and domain-wall pinning will raise coercivity relative to soft fcc FeCoNi.
The Pt-modified, L10-ordered FeCoNi alloy will have at least ten times the coercivity of the fcc FeCoNi baseline.
Pt modification and ordering may moderately reduce saturation magnetization.
The coercivity enhancement requires Pt concentration and annealing conditions that successfully produce L10 ordering.
Insufficient thermal processing may prevent formation of the ordered phase.
Composition and annealing conditions can govern phase separation or phase stability in high-entropy alloys.
Phase separation would compromise the high-entropy criterion.
Room-temperature-deposited FeCoNiMnCu films are magnetically soft, and rapid thermal annealing produces an approximately 40-fold coercivity increase while retaining an fcc phase.

In a FeCoNiMnCu-based thin film, inclusion of 50 at.% Pt followed by rapid thermal annealing produced a single L10 high-entropy intermetallic phase, high magnetic anisotropy, and an approximately three-orders-of-magnitude coercivity increase.

contradictions.description: The proposed modified alloy is called near-equiatomic FeCoNiPt, but approximately 50 at.% Pt leaves only about 16.7 at.% each of Fe, Co, and Ni. This is not near-equiatomic across the four components, although its ideal configurational entropy would still exceed 1.0R.
